outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Reinforcement Learning in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter establishes the foundational context of why Reinforcement Learning (RL) is critical for modern LLMs, specifically regarding advanced reasoning capabilities. It outlines the historical trajectory from Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to RL, highlighting the recent shift towards scaling RL for mathematical and coding tasks.
subtopics: The evolution of LLM training paradigms: From Pre-training to RLHF/RLAIF
Scaling laws in RL: Why massive computation is necessary for deep reasoning
Current landscape: Success stories vs. failure cases in scaling RL

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Foundations of Policy Optimization Algorithms
outline.description: Before delving into the proposed method, this chapter rigorously reviews existing State-of-the-Art (SOTA) algorithms. It breaks down Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), focusing on their objectives, mathematical formulations, and practical implementations.
subtopics: Notation and Problem Formulation in Autoregressive Generation
Deep dive into PPO: Role of Value Functions, Importance Ratios, and Clipping
Understanding GRPO: Eliminating Value Critics via Group-Based Advantage Estimation
Mathematical derivation of token-level versus group-relative objectives

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Diagnosing Instability in Current Methods
outline.description: This chapter identifies the root cause of 'model collapse' observed when training huge models with GRPO. It explores the theoretical flaws in applying importance sampling at the token level, demonstrating how high-variance noise accumulates over long sequences and interacts destructively with clipping mechanisms.
subtopics: The Principle of Importance Sampling: Behavior vs. Target Distributions
Why Token-Level Weighting Fails: Statistical Invalidations at Scale
"Catastrophic Collapse": Empirical evidence and irreversibility analysis
Interaction effects: How accumulation of low-quality tokens triggers divergence
